title: Additive Linear A IR hardening for source continuation across typed or unresolved physical/layout boundaries

empirical_trigger.interpretation: v1.1 remains valid for explicit cross-surface continuations and identity conflicts, but a real source may establish a continuation boundary witness without identifying whether that boundary is a physical surface transition or a ruled-line transition.

requirements: source_surface_ref and target_surface_ref are present and resolve to distinct base surfaces
boundary witness token refs may be empty only if the distinct source surfaces themselves are source-explicit
must not downgrade an unresolved witness to SURFACE
source_segment_ref and target_segment_ref are present and resolve to distinct base segments
segments must belong to the same source surface if both carry a surface_id
at least one source-native boundary witness token or explicit source line metadata must be preserved
at least one boundary_witness_token_ref resolves to a base token
each witness token type is SEPARATOR, PUNCTUATION, EDITORIAL_MARK, GAP, DAMAGE, or UNKNOWN
source_surface_ref/target_surface_ref and source_segment_ref/target_segment_ref are optional and must not manufacture a resolved boundary class

global_relation_requirements: source_group_ref and target_group_ref resolve to distinct base groups
relation adds adjacency/continuation evidence only; source-native groups remain separate
a v1.2 document also remains valid under all inherited v1.1 conflict rules

forbidden: destructively merge groups because a continuation relation exists
claim linguistic wordhood solely from this technical relation

validation_canaries: valid inherited v1.1 document with empty v1.2 continuation collection passes
valid unresolved boundary relation with a SEPARATOR witness passes
unresolved boundary with SIGN witness fails
SURFACE relation without distinct surfaces fails
LINE relation without distinct segments fails
claim-bearing view with unresolved boundary but without NO_BOUNDARY_KIND_PROMOTION fails
claim-bearing view with both fail-closed policies passes
v1.1 base regression and conflict-binding tests remain unchanged

real_projection_rule_after_admission.D5_current_cases: Encode the two lineage parts as separate SOURCE_WORD groups; preserve the intervening newline as a SEPARATOR token; use boundary_class UNRESOLVED_SURFACE_OR_LINE; do not invent surface or line IDs.
real_projection_rule_after_admission.D6_current_cases: Continue using inherited v1.1 unresolved SIGN_ID_CONFLICT bindings; v1.2 does not reclassify or semantically resolve A319/*904.
